title: 25-year-old man with a forearm abrasion
arrival: A 25-year-old man scraped his forearm against a wooden door earlier today. He has a small, superficial abrasion with no active bleeding, swelling, deformity, severe pain, or loss of movement or sensation. He is alert, comfortable, and otherwise feels well.

checkpoints.why: No stridor, respiratory distress, or central cyanosis.
His heart rate of 78 is well within range, and there is no bleeding or circulatory compromise.
He has no convulsions, and he is alert with normal mental status, so a glucose is not needed here.
A superficial abrasion is not high-risk trauma, and the limb is not threatened.
He is drinking normally, with no vomiting, diarrhoea, or bleeding.
Alert and comfortable, with no weakness and no severe pain.
The wound is superficial, and a wooden door is not an exposure requiring time-sensitive prophylaxis.
No value crosses a high-risk threshold, and he is alert on AVPU.

keyCriterion: No red, yellow, or high-risk vital sign criteria met
feedbackWhy: This patient does not meet any red or yellow criteria and has no high-risk vital signs. He can safely wait for evaluation in the low-acuity area.
reassessment: As with all patients in the waiting area, he should undergo reassessment because a patient's condition can change while waiting.
